# Lua-libghidra guidance adoption

Adapted from the workspace `saivage-instance-guidance-adoption` skill used for
PM's reviewed same-release prompt adoption. This is a host-side operator workflow,
not authority for an Executor to control its own deployment.

1. Read workspace handoff/memory, target AGENTS and workflows/OPERATIONS.md.
   Establish authorization for editing, deployment, restart, notices and ordinary
   Run separately; never infer reset, migration, provider retry or push authority.
   Verify the exact container, service, release, mounts and active child chain.
2. Edit maintained workflows/prompts at the existing policy owner. Preserve
   unrelated dirty work. Keep tools, models, identities, contracts, graphs,
   credentials and acceptance unchanged. Use the exact compatible release compiler
   and regression-test the complete affected rendered role/node closure, not only
   fragment text. Do not copy PM gameplay rules into this native Lua project.
3. Obtain independent Astra review of the same final source and composition:
   correctness, consistency, scope, ceremony and actual runtime compatibility.
   Resolve substantive findings with that reviewer. Editorial approval is not
   deployment authorization or runtime acceptance. Commit scoped source promptly.
4. Capture current chain, process results and pending effects. Use supported
   Project Stop; verify settlement, not merely a wait timeout. Under operator
   authorization stop the exact service and verify no owned descendants or runtime
   lock remain. Never erase a lock or kill a stale PID to manufacture exclusion.
5. Preserve a complete stopped backup and independent candidate, including hidden
   files, credentials, all history/records/conversations/images, work and pending
   mailboxes. Use workspace tmp; no writable hardlinks. Inventory special files:
   compare regular bytes, symlink targets, namespace/type/mode/owner separately;
   never open historical sockets/FIFOs or claim a live-process snapshot.
6. Start from deployed settings and apply only allowlisted prompt overrides.
   Use actual same-release consumers to validate saved cards/history, accepted
   records, conversations, images/work references and compiled configuration.
   Compare original and candidate results; retain preexisting limitations. A
   config-only check is insufficient. Verify every preserved path and reject
   unexpected differences or writable aliases. If migration is needed, stop and
   obtain separate authorization rather than rewriting history opportunistically.
7. Publish the reviewed complete prompt tree under exclusion, retaining displaced
   originals for rollback; do not rewrite historical roots. Restart the exact
   service; verify release, readiness, stopped execution, bindings and historical
   conversation/record/image access. Do not roll state back after resumed work.
8. Deliver authorized routine notices with normal urgency to exact owner/card
   IDs. Inspect receipts: urgent notices may stop descendants and are not a
   safe-boundary mailbox. Planner direction uses supported activate_card fields,
   not invented Planner tool permissions. With Run authorization, resume through
   Analyst's supported start_project. Observe fresh Planner/child calls and
   returned executor results; a running flag alone is not adoption evidence.
9. Record commits, review, validation, backup, allowlist, release, restart/resume
   receipts and execution evidence in workflows/OPERATIONS.md. Distinguish prompt
   adoption from product acceptance. Commit only owned source/docs, never secrets
   or runtime state; do not push without permission.
